title: The distillation double bind
authors: Alek Westover, Alexa Pan, Arun Jose (Redwood Research)
summary: Argues distilling a potentially misaligned model presents a dilemma: either misalignment transfers to the student (distillation doesn't help) or it doesn't (in which case the incriminating evidence may also not transfer).
key_result: The same mechanism that would scrub misalignment may also scrub the behavioral evidence needed to incriminate the model.
open_threads: When/whether misalignment empirically transfers under distillation; conditions under which distillation is net-safety-positive.

title: Estimating No-CoT Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models
summary: Estimates the task-completion time horizon of frontier models when not allowed chain-of-thought reasoning, complementing METR-style time-horizon work; quantifies how much capability depends on visible reasoning.
key_result: Provides estimates of how short models' effective time horizons become without CoT, informing how much monitorability/control rests on externalized reasoning.
open_threads: Generalization across task types; robustness of no-CoT elicitation; implications for control protocols assuming CoT.

title: Efficient tradeoffs and the safety-usefulness tradeoff model
summary: Develops a conceptual model of the safety-vs-usefulness tradeoff in AI control deployments, formalizing what an 'efficient' tradeoff frontier looks like for reasoning about how much usefulness must be sacrificed for given safety guarantees.
key_result: Articulates a safety-usefulness tradeoff frontier framework for evaluating and comparing control protocols.
open_threads: Empirical instantiation of the frontier; how protocol choices move along it; interaction with realistic capabilities.

title: Retrying vs Resampling in AI Control
summary: Revisits the resampling protocols from Ctrl-Z with stronger up-to-date models and compares retrying versus resampling as control strategies, evaluating which better catches untrusted-model misbehavior.
key_result: Provides an updated empirical comparison of retrying vs resampling control protocols under modern models, refining earlier Ctrl-Z findings.
open_threads: How results shift with further capability gains; protocol cost/usefulness tradeoffs; generalization.

title: Advice for making robust-to-training model organisms
authors: Alek Westover, Vivek Hebbar, Julian Stastny et al. (Redwood Research)
summary: Practical guidance for constructing model organisms of misalignment whose target behavior survives subsequent training, so they remain useful experimental testbeds.
key_result: Offers concrete techniques and pitfalls for building misalignment model organisms robust to further training.
open_threads: Generality across behaviors/models; how robust-to-training organisms relate to naturally arising misalignment.
